status_summary: EO 14192 (signed 2025-01-31) directed the Treasury Secretary and the OMB Director to reinstate the April 2018 Treasury and OMB memorandum of agreement on tax regulation review; a GAO report of 2026-07-21 states that OIRA review of tax regulations had ended in June 2023 under another agreement and was reinstated by an agreement in July 2025. A Treasury and OMB memorandum of agreement dated 2025-07-04, whose terms are known through a browser retrieval of a scanned file, provides for OIRA review of tax regulatory actions that may create a serious inconsistency with another agency's action, raise novel legal or policy issues, or have an annual non-revenue effect of 100 million dollars or more, with reviews generally concluding 45 days after OIRA receives the required information, an expedited track of up to 10 business days for implementing H.R. 1, exemptions for categories such as OFAC sanctions rules and CFIUS rules, and supersession of the 1983 agreement and rescission of the 2023-06-09 agreement; the GAO report corroborates the 45-day general review period and a 10-business-day period for regulations implementing the 2017 and 2025 tax laws. An IRS proposed rule of 2025-12-15 was recorded as not subject to section 6(b) review under the agreement, and in March 2026 one IRS proposed rule was designated for OIRA review as significant under it while another final rule was recorded as not subject to review. The arrangement is an executive agreement that can be changed.

title: Keep Treasury tax regulations under OIRA review
uncertainties: The 2025 agreement itself was not opened in readable form: the Treasury file is a scan, a direct fetch on 2026-10-22 again returned only its date line, no archive copy was found, and a further search on 2026-10-26 found no readable official copy; the Treasury Tax Regulatory Process page lists the 2025 agreement only as a link without terms. Its terms rest on the browser retrieval supplied to the project, except for features corroborated by a GAO report of 2026-07-21 opened on files.gao.gov: a general 45-day OIRA review period under the 2018 and 2025 agreements, a 10-business-day period for regulations implementing the 2017 and 2025 tax laws (the retrieval-based wording names only H.R. 1), and the end of OIRA review in June 2023 and its reinstatement by an agreement in July 2025. Footnotes in that report cite the agreement dated 2025-07-04 and the 2023 agreement dated 2023-06-09, and an IRS proposed rule of 2025-12-15 opened on govinfo.gov also confirms the 2025 agreement's date and its use. GAO describes the three review triggers and the 100 million dollar threshold as terms of the 2018 agreement and does not restate them for the 2025 agreement, so the retrieval remains the only reading of those terms in the 2025 text; the listed exclusions, the supersession and rescission paragraph and the signers were not corroborated. The 2018 agreement was read on 2026-10-26 on the White House archive (trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov): paragraph 1 sets the three triggers, including an annual non-revenue effect of 100 million dollars or more measured against a no-action baseline, paragraph 4 the 45-day and 10-business-day review periods, and paragraph 6 the supersession of the 1983 agreement. Those terms match the terms the retrieval reports for the 2025 agreement, but no term-by-term comparison with the 2025 text is possible until that text is read, so the record cannot say that the 2018 agreement was reinstated as such; the match is also consistent with the retrieval having carried 2018 language into its account of the 2025 text (inference). The typed name of the Treasury signer of the 2025 agreement is partly illegible in the scan, so signers are not recorded; the archive copy of the 2018 agreement and a Tax Notes reprint disagreed on which signer held which office, so the 2018 signers are not recorded either. The recommendation text describes the 2018 agreement and gives no thresholds of its own. Review is limited to actions meeting the three triggers and excludes listed categories, which is narrower than review of every tax regulatory action. The proportion of tax rules actually sent to OIRA was not measured.
